label_completeness.why: Nitrogenase is the only enzyme family that fixes N₂; a genome with the complete NifHDK complex very likely fixes nitrogen. The labels record the trait for only a minority of carriers, because nitrogen fixation is rarely tested and an untested trait counts as absent.

DsrAB with APS reductase is the conserved core of sulfate respiration, but the same genes run in reverse in some sulfur oxidisers (reverse-Dsr) — so part of the gap is real biology, part is missing labels.
NO reductase and N₂O reductase are committed steps of denitrification; organisms carrying both denitrify at least partly. Denitrification is under-reported in trait databases.
Photosystem II marks oxygenic photosynthesis (cyanobacteria); none of the carriers is labelled with this trait in the source database.
The PufLM reaction centre is the hallmark of anoxygenic phototrophy; almost every labelled phototroph carries it, but many carriers are not labelled.
Methanol dehydrogenase marks methylotrophs, but it is often not recorded as a trait.
The Wood–Ljungdahl pathway is also used by sulfate reducers and methanogens, so carrying it does not make an organism an acetogen — this gap is biology, not labels.
